title: Federated Learning
description: Federated learning: Privacy-preserving distributed ML. Train on decentralized data (mobile, hospital). FedAvg, secure aggregation, differential privacy. No raw data sharing.

content.level0_basic: Federated Learning: Data stays on devices (phones, hospitals), train model collaboratively. Server aggregates model updates (not raw data). Privacy-preserving. Example: Google Gboard (keyboard predictions, millions of phones), hospitals (patient data never leaves). FedAvg algorithm: (1) Server sends global model, (2) Devices train locally, (3) Send gradients/weights to server, (4) Server averages → new global model. Benefits: Privacy (GDPR, HIPAA), large-scale (billions of devices), data quality (diverse, real-world).
content.level1_beginner: FL variants: (1) Cross-device FL (millions of phones, Google, Apple), (2) Cross-silo FL (hospitals, banks, few participants). Challenges: (1) Non-IID data (each device different distribution), (2) Communication cost (bandwidth limited, compression), (3) Stragglers (slow devices, dropout), (4) Privacy attacks (gradient leakage). Solutions: FedProx (handle heterogeneity), secure aggregation (encrypted updates), differential privacy (noise addition). Communication: Gradient compression (top-k, quantization), model compression (distillation). Frameworks: TensorFlow Federated, PySyft, Flower, FedML.
content.level2_application: Applications: (1) Mobile keyboards (Gboard, SwiftKey), (2) Healthcare (hospital collaboration, rare diseases), (3) Finance (fraud detection, banks), (4) IoT (smart home, edge devices). Deployment: On-device training (TFLite, CoreML), server aggregation (secure MPC), differential privacy (ε-DP). Production: Google, Apple (privacy by design), NVIDIA Clara (healthcare FL). Cross-silo: 10-100 organizations (hospitals, banks). Privacy tech: Homomorphic encryption, secure multi-party computation.
content.level3_advanced: Advanced: (1) Personalization (local fine-tuning + global model), (2) Asynchronous FL (no sync wait), (3) Hierarchical FL (edge-cloud), (4) Incentive mechanisms (contribution reward), (5) Fairness (underrepresented groups), (6) Robustness (Byzantine attacks, poisoning). Research: Split learning, vertical FL (different features), transfer FL, continual FL (lifelong learning).
content.level4_expert: Production systems: Model versioning, client selection (biased sampling), convergence guarantees (non-convex), communication-efficient protocols, privacy auditing (membership inference defense), regulatory compliance (GDPR Article 25). Hardware: Edge TPU, secure enclaves (TEE). Scale: 10M+ devices. Research frontiers: Zero-knowledge FL, blockchain-based FL, quantum-secure FL.

whatIsIt: Federated Learning: Core concept with mathematical formulation.
whyNeeded: Federated Learning addresses critical challenges in modern ML systems.
realWorldAnalogy: Federated Learning explained through intuitive real-world analogy.

formulas: \text{FedAvg}: \quad w_{t+1} = \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{n_k}{n} w_k^t \quad \text{(weighted average of client models)}
\text{Differential Privacy}: \quad \mathcal{M}(D) \text{ is } (\epsilon, \delta)\text{-DP if } P(\mathcal{M}(D) \in S) \leq e^\epsilon P(\mathcal{M}(D') \in S) + \delta
\text{Communication Cost}: \quad C = R \cdot K \cdot |w| \quad \text{(R=rounds, K=clients, |w|=model size)}

stepByStep: 1. **Server Init**: Global model w_0'yu başlat (örn: ResNet, BERT), tüm client'lara gönder
2. **Client Selection**: K client'tan rastgele m tanesini seç (m << K, örn: 100/10000), non-IID veri dağılımını dengele
3. **Local Training**: Her seçilen client k, local veri D_k üzerinde E epoch SGD: w_k^{t+1} = w^t - η∇L_k(w^t)
4. **Model Upload**: Client'lar güncellenmiş ağırlık w_k^{t+1} (veya gradyent Δw_k)'i server'a gönder (encrypted, compressed)
5. **Secure Aggregation**: Server, client güncellemelerini weighted average ile birleştir: w^{t+1} = Σ (n_k/n)w_k^{t+1}, n_k=client k'nın veri sayısı
6. **Global Model Update**: Yeni global model w^{t+1}'i tüm client'lara broadcast et, T round tekrarla → Convergence
algorithm.complexity: Communication: O(R·K·|w|) total (R rounds, K clients, |w| model size). Compression: Top-k sparsification O(k) per client. Computation: O(E·|D_k|·|w|) per client (E local epochs). Privacy: Secure aggregation O(K²) (multi-party computation). Convergence: O(1/√(m·R)) for non-IID data (m clients per round).

codeExamples.title: FedAvg (Federated Averaging) from Scratch
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Subset
import copy

class SimpleCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(1, 32, 3), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2))
        self.fc = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(32*13*13, 128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(128, 10))
    
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.fc(self.conv(x).flatten(1))

def federated_averaging(global_model, client_datasets, n_rounds=10, n_clients_per_round=5, local_epochs=5, lr=0.01):
    """FedAvg: Privacy-preserving distributed training"""
    
    for round_idx in range(n_rounds):
        print(f"\n=== Round {round_idx+1}/{n_rounds} ===")
        
        # Step 1: Server broadcasts global model to clients
        global_weights = copy.deepcopy(global_model.state_dict())
        
        # Step 2: Random client selection (simulate device availability)
        selected_clients = torch.randperm(len(client_datasets))[:n_clients_per_round]
        
        client_weights = []
        client_data_sizes = []
        
        # Step 3: Each client trains locally on private data
        for client_id in selected_clients:
            print(f"  Client {client_id}: Local training...")
            
            # Local model (copy of global)
            local_model = SimpleCNN()
            local_model.load_state_dict(global_weights)
            optimizer = optim.SGD(local_model.parameters(), lr=lr)
            
            # Train on client's private data (never leaves device!)
            train_loader = DataLoader(client_datasets[client_id], batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
            local_model.train()
            for epoch in range(local_epochs):
                for X, y in train_loader:
                    optimizer.zero_grad()
                    loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(local_model(X), y)
                    loss.backward()
                    optimizer.step()
            
            # Step 4: Send updated weights to server (encrypted in production)
            client_weights.append(copy.deepcopy(local_model.state_dict()))
            client_data_sizes.append(len(client_datasets[client_id]))
        
        # Step 5: Server aggregates (weighted average by data size)
        total_data = sum(client_data_sizes)
        aggregated_weights = {}
        for key in global_weights.keys():
            # w_global = Σ (n_k / n_total) * w_k
            aggregated_weights[key] = sum(
                (client_data_sizes[i] / total_data) * client_weights[i][key]
                for i in range(len(client_weights))
            )
        
        # Step 6: Update global model
        global_model.load_state_dict(aggregated_weights)
        
        # Evaluate global model
        acc = evaluate_global(global_model, test_loader)
        print(f"  Global model accuracy: {acc:.2%}")
    
    return global_model

# Simulate federated setting: 100 clients with non-IID data
global_model = SimpleCNN()

# Split MNIST into 100 clients (non-IID: each client has 2 digits)
full_dataset = torchvision.datasets.MNIST(root='./data', train=True, download=True)
client_datasets = []
for client_id in range(100):
    # Non-IID: client gets only 2 digit classes
    digit_classes = [(client_id * 2) % 10, (client_id * 2 + 1) % 10]
    indices = [i for i, (_, label) in enumerate(full_dataset) if label in digit_classes]
    client_datasets.append(Subset(full_dataset, indices[:500]))  # 500 samples per client

# Federated training (data never leaves clients!)
final_model = federated_averaging(
    global_model,
    client_datasets,
    n_rounds=20,
    n_clients_per_round=10,  # Only 10% participate per round
    local_epochs=5,
    lr=0.01
)

print(f"\nFinal test accuracy: {evaluate_global(final_model, test_loader):.2%}")
print("Privacy preserved: Raw data never left devices!")
codeExamples.explanation: FedAvg (Federated Averaging): Google'ın 2017 algoritması. Server global model broadcast → Client'lar local data'da train (privacy!) → Server weighted average ile aggregate. Non-IID data: Her client farklı dağılım (örn: her telefon farklı kullanıcı). Production: Secure aggregation (homomorphic encryption), differential privacy (gradient'e noise), communication efficiency (gradient compression).

codeExamples.title: Differential Privacy in Federated Learning
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import numpy as np

class DPFederatedLearning:
    """Federated Learning with Differential Privacy (DP-SGD)"""
    def __init__(self, model, epsilon=1.0, delta=1e-5, max_grad_norm=1.0):
        self.model = model
        self.epsilon = epsilon  # Privacy budget
        self.delta = delta      # Failure probability
        self.max_grad_norm = max_grad_norm
        self.noise_multiplier = self._compute_noise_multiplier()
    
    def _compute_noise_multiplier(self):
        """σ for (ε,δ)-DP: σ ≥ √(2·log(1.25/δ)) / ε"""
        return np.sqrt(2 * np.log(1.25 / self.delta)) / self.epsilon
    
    def clip_gradients(self, gradients):
        """Clip per-sample gradients: g' = g / max(1, ||g||_2 / C)"""
        total_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(gradients, self.max_grad_norm)
        return total_norm
    
    def add_noise(self, aggregated_grad):
        """Add Gaussian noise: g_noisy = g + N(0, σ²C²I)"""
        noise_std = self.noise_multiplier * self.max_grad_norm
        noise = torch.normal(0, noise_std, size=aggregated_grad.shape)
        return aggregated_grad + noise
    
    def private_aggregate(self, client_gradients, client_data_sizes):
        """Aggregate with DP: (1) Clip, (2) Average, (3) Add noise"""
        # Step 1: Clip each client's gradient (bound sensitivity)
        clipped_grads = []
        for grad in client_gradients:
            with torch.no_grad():
                norm = torch.norm(torch.cat([g.flatten() for g in grad]))
                clip_factor = min(1.0, self.max_grad_norm / (norm + 1e-6))
                clipped = [g * clip_factor for g in grad]
            clipped_grads.append(clipped)
        
        # Step 2: Weighted average
        total_data = sum(client_data_sizes)
        aggregated = {}
        for param_idx in range(len(clipped_grads[0])):
            aggregated[param_idx] = sum(
                (client_data_sizes[i] / total_data) * clipped_grads[i][param_idx]
                for i in range(len(clipped_grads))
            )
        
        # Step 3: Add calibrated Gaussian noise
        noisy_grads = [self.add_noise(g) for g in aggregated.values()]
        
        return noisy_grads

# Usage: Federated learning with privacy guarantee
model = SimpleCNN()
dp_fl = DPFederatedLearning(model, epsilon=1.0, delta=1e-5)  # (1.0, 1e-5)-DP

for round_idx in range(20):
    client_gradients = []  # Collected from clients
    client_data_sizes = []
    
    for client_id in selected_clients:
        # Client computes gradient locally
        local_grad = compute_client_gradient(model, client_datasets[client_id])
        client_gradients.append(local_grad)
        client_data_sizes.append(len(client_datasets[client_id]))
    
    # Server aggregates with DP
    noisy_grad = dp_fl.private_aggregate(client_gradients, client_data_sizes)
    
    # Update global model with DP gradient
    with torch.no_grad():
        for param, grad in zip(model.parameters(), noisy_grad):
            param -= 0.01 * grad  # SGD step
    
    print(f"Round {round_idx}: Privacy budget spent: ε={dp_fl.epsilon:.2f}, δ={dp_fl.delta:.2e}")

# Privacy guarantee: No individual client data can be inferred!
print(f"\nPrivacy guarantee: ({dp_fl.epsilon}, {dp_fl.delta})-Differential Privacy")
print(f"Interpretation: Attacker cannot distinguish if any single client participated.")
codeExamples.explanation: Differential Privacy (DP): Client gradient'lerine noise ekleyerek bireysel veri gizliliğini garantile. (ε,δ)-DP: ε küçük → güçlü privacy (ama accuracy düşer), δ failure probability. DP-SGD: (1) Gradient clipping (sensitivity bound), (2) Gaussian noise ekleme (σ = √(2log(1.25/δ))/ε). Production: Apple, Google DP kullanır (ε=1-8). Tradeoff: Privacy ↔ Accuracy (noise artarsa accuracy düşer). Privacy accounting: Composition theorem (T round → ε_total = √(2T·log(1/δ))·ε).

codeExamples.title: Communication-Efficient FL (Gradient Compression)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import numpy as np

class GradientCompression:
    """Reduce communication cost: Top-k sparsification + quantization"""
    def __init__(self, compression_ratio=0.01, quantization_bits=8):
        self.compression_ratio = compression_ratio  # Keep top 1% gradients
        self.quantization_bits = quantization_bits
    
    def topk_sparsification(self, gradients):
        """Keep only top-k largest gradients (by magnitude)"""
        flat_grad = torch.cat([g.flatten() for g in gradients])
        k = int(len(flat_grad) * self.compression_ratio)
        
        # Select top-k by absolute value
        topk_values, topk_indices = torch.topk(flat_grad.abs(), k)
        signs = torch.sign(flat_grad[topk_indices])
        
        # Sparse representation: (indices, values)
        sparse_grad = {
            'indices': topk_indices.cpu().numpy(),
            'values': (topk_values * signs).cpu().numpy(),
            'shape': flat_grad.shape
        }
        
        # Communication reduction
        original_size = flat_grad.numel() * 4  # 32-bit float
        compressed_size = k * 8  # indices (4B) + values (4B)
        print(f"  Compression: {original_size/1e6:.2f}MB → {compressed_size/1e6:.2f}MB ({compressed_size/original_size:.1%})")
        
        return sparse_grad
    
    def quantize(self, values, bits=8):
        """Quantize gradients to lower precision (32-bit → 8-bit)"""
        # Linear quantization: x_q = round((2^b - 1) * (x - min) / (max - min))
        v_min, v_max = values.min(), values.max()
        scale = (2**bits - 1) / (v_max - v_min + 1e-8)
        quantized = torch.round((values - v_min) * scale).to(torch.uint8)
        
        # Dequantization parameters
        return {
            'quantized': quantized.cpu().numpy(),
            'scale': scale.item(),
            'min': v_min.item()
        }
    
    def decompress(self, sparse_grad, original_shapes):
        """Reconstruct gradient from sparse representation"""
        flat_grad = torch.zeros(sparse_grad['shape'])
        flat_grad[torch.tensor(sparse_grad['indices'])] = torch.tensor(sparse_grad['values'])
        
        # Reshape back to original
        reconstructed = []
        offset = 0
        for shape in original_shapes:
            numel = np.prod(shape)
            reconstructed.append(flat_grad[offset:offset+numel].view(shape))
            offset += numel
        
        return reconstructed

# Federated learning with compression (100x less communication!)
compressor = GradientCompression(compression_ratio=0.01, quantization_bits=8)

for round_idx in range(20):
    compressed_updates = []
    
    for client_id in selected_clients:
        # Client trains locally
        local_model = train_local(client_datasets[client_id], epochs=5)
        
        # Compute weight update (Δw = w_new - w_old)
        delta_w = [new - old for new, old in zip(local_model.parameters(), global_model.parameters())]
        
        # Compress before sending (critical for mobile networks!)
        sparse_update = compressor.topk_sparsification(delta_w)
        quantized_update = compressor.quantize(torch.tensor(sparse_update['values']))
        
        compressed_updates.append({
            'sparse': sparse_update,
            'quantized': quantized_update,
            'client_id': client_id
        })
    
    # Server decompresses and aggregates
    decompressed_updates = [compressor.decompress(u['sparse'], [p.shape for p in global_model.parameters()]) 
                            for u in compressed_updates]
    
    # FedAvg aggregation
    aggregated = [sum(updates) / len(updates) for updates in zip(*decompressed_updates)]
    
    # Update global model
    with torch.no_grad():
        for param, delta in zip(global_model.parameters(), aggregated):
            param += delta

print("Communication cost reduced by ~100x (1% sparsity + 8-bit quantization)!")
print("Mobile-friendly: 10MB → 0.1MB per round per client")
codeExamples.explanation: Communication Efficiency: FL'in en büyük bottleneck'i bandwidth (özellikle mobile). Solutions: (1) Gradient sparsification (top-k: sadece en büyük k gradient'i gönder, %99 sıfır), (2) Quantization (32-bit → 8-bit), (3) Sketching (random projection). Production: FedAvg + compression → 100x daha az data transfer. Tradeoff: Compression ↔ Convergence speed (sparse gradient → daha yavaş converge, ama communication efficient). Mobile deployment kritik: 4G/5G upload limited, battery drain.

quiz.question: What is Federated Learning?
options: Centralized training on server with all data
Decentralized ML: Train on client devices, share only model updates (not raw data). Privacy-preserving
quiz.explanation: Federated Learning: Train ML models across distributed devices (phones, hospitals) without centralizing data. Each client trains locally, sends gradient updates to server. Server aggregates (FedAvg) → global model. Privacy: Raw data never leaves device.

quiz.question: What is the main challenge in Federated Learning?
options: Non-IID data (clients have different distributions), communication cost, stragglers
quiz.explanation: FL Challenges: (1) Non-IID: Client A has cat images, Client B dogs → distribution skew. (2) Communication: Bandwidth limited (mobile), expensive. (3) Stragglers: Slow clients delay rounds. (4) Privacy attacks: Gradient inversion. Solutions: FedProx, compression, async aggregation.

flashcards.back: Decentralized ML training on client devices. Share model updates (gradients), not raw data. Privacy-preserving. FedAvg aggregation on server. Use case: Mobile keyboards, healthcare.
Clients have non-identical distributions (hospital A: mostly diabetes, B: cancer). Causes model divergence. Solution: FedProx (proximal term), personalization (local fine-tune).
Server aggregates client model updates: w_global = Σ(n_k/n)·w_k (weighted by data size). Clients train local epochs (E=5), then upload Δw. Communication-efficient.

commonMistakes.mistake: Sending raw data to server instead of gradients
commonMistakes.why: Defeats FL purpose: Privacy violation. Raw data should never leave client device
commonMistakes.fix: Only send model weight updates (Δw = w_new - w_old) or gradients. Differential privacy (DP) noise if needed.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not handling stragglers (slow clients blocking rounds)
commonMistakes.why: Synchronous FedAvg waits for all clients → 1 slow client delays entire round (network latency, low battery)
commonMistakes.fix: Use asynchronous aggregation (FedAsync) or timeout (drop stragglers after T seconds). Monitor client latency distribution.

commonMistakes.mistake: Ignoring non-IID data (assuming clients have same distribution)
commonMistakes.why: Non-IID → model divergence (each client pulls global model to its local distribution). Poor generalization
commonMistakes.fix: Use FedProx (μ·||w - w_global||² regularization) or personalization (local fine-tune after global training). Data augmentation.
